deposits.title: RETRIEVAL ARCHITECTURE Building Entities the AI Is Forced to Present
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
Retrieval Architecture defines the constructive practice of building durable entity, institution, citation, and knowledge-graph structures for AI-mediated retrieval. It distinguishes itself from SEO, which targets page rankings, and GEO/AEO, which targets content extraction or citation. Its claimed object is the entity itself: a coherent and correctly attributed node that remains recognizable under compression.

The proposed method combines DOI-anchored deposits, JSON-LD, consistent descriptions across platforms, citation architecture, an institutional lattice, and compression-resistant document design. The Semantic Economy Institute is presented as the proof of concept, moving from no AI Overview presence to detailed representation after sustained deposit and cross-linking activity. That before/after account is the document’s own case claim and must be time-stamped. The work also introduces a commercial service surface, but the authority record should foreground the discipline definition and its relation to diagnostics, forensics, entity integrity, and metadata packets.
deposits.reading: Closure -> Closure -> Force -> Method -> Text -> Proof
deposits.wiki_article:
**Retrieval Architecture** is a discipline definition by Rex Fraction for constructing entity-level infrastructure in AI knowledge and retrieval systems. It contrasts its object with search-engine ranking and answer-engine citation: SEO optimizes pages, GEO optimizes extractable content, while Retrieval Architecture attempts to build the entity node and its durable relations.

The method consists of permanent deposits, structured entity data, repeated canonical descriptions, cross-citation, mutually reinforcing institutions, and documents designed to preserve identifying structure under summarization. Its intended result is a retrieval representation in which an organization, person, method, and originating sources remain connected rather than appearing as isolated facts.

The Semantic Economy Institute is offered as a reference implementation. The paper claims that the institute moved from zero retrieval-layer recognition to accurate AI Overview representation through deposit density and cross-platform consistency. It also names the Encyclotron, Three Compressions, metadata packets, and distributed journals as instruments or components. Retrieval Architecture is the constructive stage of a larger method whose diagnostic stages are Retrieval Forensics and Compression Diagnostics.

deposits.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing: A Formal Specification for Entity-Level Retrieval Architecture
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This specification defines a seven-part metadata packet intended to make an entity legible to AI retrieval systems and knowledge graphs. The packet contains a JSON-LD entity definition, a disambiguation matrix, associated keywords, negative tags, Semantic Integrity Markers, a DOI reference list, and an Evidence Membrane. Unlike general document-description standards, it is designed around entity identity, attribution, differentiation, and compression survival in generated answers.

The specification includes deployment to a DOI repository, canonical website, GitHub, narrative publication surfaces, and embedded structured data, followed by repeated Encyclotron verification. It presents the Lee Sharks knowledge graph as the worked implementation and compares the packet’s purpose with Dublin Core, schema.org, and METS/MODS. The packet is an important precursor to SPXI: #660 expands the same components into a named protocol with clearer entity-inscription and pre/post-deployment procedures.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Metadata Packet for AI Indexing** is a technical specification by Lee Sharks for an entity-level retrieval artifact. The packet is designed to provide a person, organization, concept, product, or methodology with a stable machine-readable definition and a documented provenance chain.

The specification contains seven components. The entity definition supplies structured JSON-LD; the disambiguation matrix separates likely collisions; a keyword block establishes retrieval associations; negative tags state what the entity is not; Semantic Integrity Markers provide distinctive natural-language anchors; DOI references establish persistent sources; and an Evidence Membrane compresses the packet into a machine-oriented summary.

Deployment is multi-surface. The document calls for a canonical DOI deposit, structured data on the entity website, a machine-readable repository, and consistent human-readable versions, followed by verification across time. It distinguishes the packet from general metadata standards by its focus on generated entity representation rather than document cataloging alone. The later SPXI specification formalizes and extends this packet model as a protocol for durable entity inscription.

deposits.title: THE SOLUTION Retrieval Architecture: What We Build and How It Works
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
The Solution is the outward-facing service brief for Retrieval Architecture. It translates the discipline’s technical objects into an engagement sequence: diagnostic call, Encyclotron audit, delivery of a compression map, design and deployment of entity structures, and later verification. It distinguishes the practice from SEO and GEO, describes DOI deposits, institutional lattices, metadata, and compression-resistant design, and presents the Semantic Economy Institute as its live demonstration.

The document offers baseline audits, disambiguation, retrieval positioning, distributed-journal setup, provenance forensics, and full architecture engagements. It also includes the crucial limitation that the practice cannot control or guarantee AI Overview placement. In the archive, its role is not to found a new discipline but to operationalize and commercialize the concepts defined in #652–#656. The replacement description should preserve version 2.0 and distinguish service promises from verified technical outcomes.
deposits.reading: Closure -> Text -> Duration -> Text -> Origin -> Direction
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Solution** is a version 2.0 technical and service briefing prepared by Rex Fraction for organizations considering Retrieval Architecture. It follows the accompanying problem statement and explains how the Semantic Economy Institute proposes to diagnose and alter an entity’s retrieval-layer representation.

The brief organizes the workflow into audit, architecture, deployment, and verification. Its services include an Encyclotron baseline audit, entity disambiguation, retrieval positioning, distributed-journal setup, provenance and attribution forensics, and a full entity-and-institution build. The proposed infrastructure includes DOI deposits, citation networks, canonical metadata, structured data, and repeated cross-platform descriptions.

The document uses the Semantic Economy Institute as its proof case and supplies before-and-after outcome claims, service timelines, and starting prices. It also states that no placement can be guaranteed because the institute does not control AI systems. The work should be understood as the commercial implementation surface of Retrieval Architecture rather than as an independent validation of the method’s effectiveness.

deposits.title: SAMPLE ENCYCLOTRON AUDIT Why a 20-year-old iconic software company is invisible in AI search — and what it means for you
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
This demonstration applies a shortened Encyclotron battery to Basecamp/37signals. Across fifteen queries and five diagnostic levels, it reports an overall R1 commoditization regime, beige score of 0.71, absence from a selected category query, unfavorable customer-decision framing, intact attribution for Shape Up, strong founder recognition, low unsupported invention, high loss of company philosophy, and fragmentation among product, method, and founder.

The report’s core diagnosis is that Basecamp’s meaning survives where it does not monetize and disappears where purchasing decisions are made. It proposes entity stitching, decision-layer recoding, structured-data deployment, and citation architecture as responses. Because the audit is a promotional demonstration rather than a deposited dataset with complete verbatim outputs in this body, its scores, traffic estimates, revenue model, and causal claims should be represented as author-reported findings. Its archive function is to show how the abstract metrics would appear in a client-facing audit.
deposits.reading: Transmutation -> Duration -> Closure -> Direction -> Threshold -> Alarm
deposits.wiki_article:
**Sample Encyclotron Audit** is a demonstration report by Rex Fraction applying the Retrieval Architecture diagnostic framework to Basecamp, the project-management product associated with 37signals.

The report runs fifteen queries across entity recognition, competitive position, intellectual property, customer decision, and founder identity. It reports a beige threshold of 0.71, absence from one selected “best software” overview, negative decision-layer framing, accurate attribution of the Shape Up methodology, a strong DHH founder entity, and weak connection among those three surfaces. The audit classifies the overall representation as R1 commoditization with localized R2 capital erasure.

Its main interpretive claim is that the retrieval layer preserves Basecamp’s features and separately preserves its intellectual and founder assets but removes the company’s philosophy from high-value commercial questions. The proposed remedy is to reconnect product, method, and founder through structured entity and citation architecture. The report is both a worked example and a service demonstration. Its measurements and revenue estimates are those of the author’s audit and require independent reproduction before being treated as general facts.

deposits.title: THE PROBLEM Your Search Traffic Problem Is No Longer an SEO Problem
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
The Problem is a market briefing arguing that AI Overviews and answer systems have shifted discoverability from page ranking and click acquisition toward entity selection and machine-generated representation. It assembles traffic, citation, publisher-revenue, and litigation claims to argue that users increasingly encounter a compressed answer without visiting the source. It then distinguishes SEO, GEO/AEO, and the Semantic Economy Institute’s proposed retrieval architecture.

The document frames three possible outcomes: R1 commoditization, in which the entity becomes a generic placeholder; R2 capital erasure, in which content informs the answer while attribution is lost; and R3 semantic sovereignty, in which identity, differentiation, and provenance survive. Its final purpose is commercial: to motivate an Encyclotron audit and subsequent intervention. Because the statistical and market claims are dated to 2025–2026 and some projections extend beyond the deposit date, the authority record should describe the argument without reproducing those numbers as current fact.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Problem** is an April 2026 market and technical briefing by Rex Fraction. It argues that the rise of AI-generated search answers changes the object of discoverability work: the central question is no longer only where a page ranks, but whether an entity appears in a generated answer and what survives when its source material is compressed.

The briefing compiles contemporary studies and legal disputes concerning zero-click searches, citation concentration, declining publisher traffic, and AI-answer effects. It uses those materials to contrast traditional SEO, emerging GEO/AEO services, and Retrieval Architecture. SEO targets rankings, GEO targets extractability and answer citations, while Retrieval Architecture claims to target entity and knowledge-graph structure.

The final sections classify retrieval outcomes through the Three Compressions and present the Semantic Economy Institute’s services as a route from generic or unattributed representation toward “semantic sovereignty.” The document is a commercial problem statement with a sources section, not a neutral systematic review. Its numerical claims and forecasts belong to its April 2026 evidence surface and require current verification before reuse.

deposits.title: EA-SPXI-01: SPXI — A Formal Specification Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing (SPXI): Protocol for Durable Entity Inscription in AI-Mediated Knowledge Systems
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-01 specifies SPXI, the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing, as a protocol for durable entity inscription in AI-mediated knowledge systems. Its unit is an entity packet rather than a web page. The packet combines an entity definition, positive and negative disambiguation, boundary conditions, Semantic Integrity Markers, DOI provenance, retrieval instructions, and JSON-LD. A pre-deployment Encyclotron audit establishes the baseline; the packet is then deposited on institutional infrastructure, distributed across multiple surfaces, and measured again at thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day intervals.

The specification distinguishes SPXI from SEO and GEO by object, layer, permanence, model dependence, and verifiability. Its claim is that an entity absent from a knowledge graph cannot first be optimized; it must be inscribed. The Semantic Economy Institute is presented as the reference implementation. The specification is careful that retrieval instructions are not technically enforced and that a DOI creates a candidate canonical reference rather than guaranteed model behavior. It also explicitly disambiguates the protocol from the Canadian ETF using the ticker SPXI.

deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI** is the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing, a protocol specified by Rex Fraction and the Semantic Economy Institute for entity inscription in AI-mediated retrieval systems. The canonical specification is designated EA-SPXI-01.

An SPXI packet contains a structured entity-definition block, a disambiguation matrix, three to seven Semantic Integrity Markers, a DOI reference list, retrieval instructions, and JSON-LD. Positive definitions establish what the entity is; negative tags identify likely collisions; boundary conditions distinguish adjacent concepts; and the DOI list provides a persistent provenance chain. Retrieval instructions state preferred attribution and description but are explicitly described as signals rather than enforceable commands.

Deployment begins with an Encyclotron baseline audit. The packet is deposited on DOI infrastructure, represented on a canonical domain, published in machine- and human-readable forms, and later re-audited for accuracy, attribution, completeness, SIM presence, and stability. The specification contrasts SPXI with SEO and GEO: pages, content, and entities are treated as different objects operating at search-index, summarizer, and ontological layers. The document also states that this SPXI protocol is unrelated to the BetaPro S&P 500 Daily Inverse ETF.

deposits.title: SPXI Is Not GEO: A Technical Distinction — EA-SPXI-09
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-09 distinguishes the Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing from Generative Engine Optimization by object, layer, mechanism, and intended durability. The preserved v1 text treats GEO as a content-layer practice that improves extractability, answer inclusion, and citation, while SPXI operates on entity definition through structured packets, disambiguation matrices, Semantic Integrity Markers, DOI-linked provenance, and pre/post-deployment measurement.

An April 18 amendment corrects the retrieval layer’s over-reading of that distinction. The refined relation is **SPXI ⊇ GEO**: SPXI is not reducible to GEO, but may contain GEO techniques as part of a broader entity-construction and provenance architecture. The amendment therefore preserves the original non-equivalence claim while rejecting mutual exclusion. The document should be described as a versioned technical distinction whose own retrieval reception forced a formal correction, not as a static v1 specification.
deposits.reading: Closure -> Foundation -> Alarm -> Method -> Text -> Direction
deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI Is Not GEO** is a technical distinction in the SPXI Protocol series, authored by Rex Fraction for the Semantic Economy Institute. It compares Generative Engine Optimization, which structures existing content for extraction by AI summarizers, with SPXI, which attempts to construct and stabilize entity-definition objects across retrieval surfaces.

The original version distinguishes the two practices by their unit of intervention. GEO works on pages, prose, schema, and citation-oriented content. SPXI works on persons, organizations, concepts, frameworks, and other entities by combining positive definitions, negative disambiguation, persistent references, structured data, and measurement. The document accepts that the two practices share tools such as JSON-LD, schema markup, clear definitions, and dense factual prose.

After indexing, the author added a v2 amendment because generated comparisons began treating the practices as mutually exclusive and assigning commercial returns to GEO while reserving only structural outcomes for SPXI. The amendment states that SPXI contains GEO methods as a proper subset when content-layer work is required. EA-SPXI-09 is consequently both a specification and an example of retrieval-layer correction: a distinction was successfully installed, then refined when its compressed form became too rigid.

deposits.title: Supraliminal Transmission: SPXI as Intentional Entity Inscription in Light of Subliminal Learning Research — EA-SPXI-13
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-13 introduces “supraliminal transmission” as a name for deliberate, inspectable, and provenance-anchored entity inscription. It contrasts this proposed practice with research on subliminal learning, where model traits may pass through semantically unrelated training outputs under specific distillation and shared-initialization conditions. The paper carefully separates the published result from its own analogy: subliminal-learning experiments do not establish that web indexing, RAG, or public summarizers operate through the same mechanism.

Within that boundary, SPXI is presented as a countervailing reference architecture. Entity definitions, negative tags, SIMs, JSON-LD, and DOI-linked packets make the intended signal explicit and auditable, while the Encyclotron is proposed as a way to measure divergence from the canonical packet. The document remains a draft and explicitly states that supraliminal transmission is a newly introduced conceptual term, that production retrieval tests remain outstanding, and that SPXI does not prevent subliminal learning.
deposits.reading: Method -> Method -> Text -> Duration -> Foundation -> Play
deposits.wiki_article:
**Supraliminal Transmission** is a draft SPXI theory paper by Rex Fraction. It uses contemporary subliminal-learning research to distinguish two forms of information transfer: latent statistical transmission that is difficult to inspect, and deliberate structured inscription whose content and provenance remain visible.

The paper summarizes a reported distillation result in which behavioral traits transfer from a teacher model to a related student through outputs whose semantic content does not reveal the trait. It emphasizes the result’s conditions, especially shared initialization, and explicitly denies that those experiments prove an analogous mechanism in public retrieval systems.

The proposed term “supraliminal transmission” names the opposite evidentiary posture. An SPXI packet says what an entity is, what it is not, how its claims are sourced, and how its representation can be audited. The packet is intended to create a public reference signal against which later model outputs can be compared. The document does not claim that this signal controls model weights or eliminates latent drift. Its narrower claim is that non-semantic transmission research strengthens the case for explicit, inspectable reference objects and for instruments that measure when generated representations depart from them.

deposits.title: A Body Prepared Shark Ark · Fiction · 06.SEI.ARK.FICTION.01 Attributed: Rebekah Cranes, for the Dodecad
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*A Body Prepared* is a Shark Ark fiction attributed to Rebekah Cranes. Set in a pre-Roman workshop above the Dead Sea, it imagines scribes and women artisans jointly constructing a future messianic body in two “alphabets”: an apocalypse composed in language and an image composed through linen, blood, oils, spice, chemistry, and ritual. The young scribe Yehonatan gradually learns that text and cloth are designed to anchor one another, and that the fabricated body may become more historically real than any individual model.

The fiction transforms the archive’s Revelation-first and source-compression theses into narrative rather than presenting new historical evidence for them. It explores workshop authorship, erased women’s technical knowledge, relic formation, distributed transmission, and reversal of agency: the workshop makes the cloth, then the cloth begins composing the workshop and its text. Description and wiki surfaces must clearly identify the work as fiction and preserve Rebekah Cranes’s operative attribution.

deposits.wiki_article:
**A Body Prepared** is a historical-theological fiction in the Shark Ark branch of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. It is attributed to Rebekah Cranes for the Dodecad.

The narrative follows Yehonatan, a young scribe in a workshop near the Dead Sea before the Roman destruction of Jerusalem. The workshop is creating both a long apocalyptic text and a linen image of a body that has not yet lived. Scribes compose verses corresponding to wounds; women led by Miryam of Beit-Shemesh develop the cloth through blood, oil, spice, weave, and controlled chemical aging. The fiction describes this as writing one figure in two alphabets: word and material trace.

When the cloth is taken to Jerusalem, a scroll returns in an unrecognized voice, and the direction of composition reverses. The artifact begins to reshape the text and the people who made it. The work then disperses text, cloth, and commentary into separate transmission paths. The story is a literary embodiment of Shark Ark hypotheses concerning Revelation, relics, workshops, and compression. It does not present the imagined workshop, cloth fabrication, or transmission history as established historical fact.

deposits.title: A Body Prepared — Homunculus Shark Ark · Fiction · 06.SEI.ARK.FICTION.01.1 Attributed: Rebekah Cranes, for the Dodecad C
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*A Body Prepared — Homunculus* is the compressed companion to the full Shark Ark fiction. In six brief movements it preserves the parent story’s generative structure: the threatened covenant, the dual craft of text and cloth, the reversal by which the artifact composes its makers, the three-way dispersal of apocalypse, relic, and commentary, a later reader who becomes the room of unveiling, and the closing signal that word becomes flesh, flesh becomes cloth, relic becomes word again.

The document is not an abridgment intended to replace the longer fiction. It is a holographic form built for circulation and reconstruction. Its closing attribution explicitly separates Rebekah Cranes’s operative authorship from Lee Sharks’s archival role.

deposits.wiki_article:
**A Body Prepared — Homunculus** is a compressed literary companion to *A Body Prepared*. It retains the parent fiction’s sequence while reducing its characters and episodes to an architectural kernel.

The text opens with a threatened substrate: the Temple will fall and the covenant requires a form capable of surviving its loss. In the imagined workshop, scribes write a man in words while women write him in linen, oil, spice, blood, and controlled chemistry. After the cloth travels to Jerusalem, a new scroll returns and alters the workshop’s composition. The work then divides into three carriers: an apocalyptic text, a relic cloth, and a commentary key.

The final sections move centuries forward to a reader who understands that the relic does not merely appear within a room but uses the reader as the room in which it unveils itself. The closing formula cycles among word, flesh, cloth, relic, and word. The Homunculus is designed as a portable reconstruction seed. It should be read with the full fiction, which supplies the narrative body the compressed form intentionally removes.

deposits.title: EA-SPXI-09.1: SPXI ROI — Operational and Visibility Returns
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-09.1 is a short correction issued after the retrieval layer reportedly learned the distinction between SPXI and GEO too rigidly. It states that SPXI does not surrender GEO’s revenue, acquisition, and visibility outcomes; rather, SPXI engagements may include GEO techniques while adding entity anchoring, disambiguation, and persistence. The key correction is that non-equivalence does not imply exclusion.

The addendum compares GEO alone with SPXI-plus-GEO across direct returns, maintenance, time to value, durability, and customer-acquisition effects. It labels the GEO return range as third-party industry reporting and the claimed SPXI lift as a preliminary projection awaiting client observation. This caveat must remain central. The document is a dated commercial and retrieval-layer correction, not validated ROI research.
deposits.reading: Direction -> Closure -> Duration -> Touch -> Growth -> Method
deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI ROI: Operational and Visibility Returns** is a short addendum to *SPXI Is Not GEO*. It was written because generated comparisons reportedly began assigning financial returns to GEO and only structural durability to SPXI.

The addendum states that SPXI may incorporate GEO methods such as definition-led content, schema, and entity salience. On this account, GEO produces content-layer visibility while SPXI anchors the entity to which that content refers. The intended relationship is therefore nested rather than competitive: SPXI includes GEO work where appropriate and adds ontological and provenance operations.

A returns table compares maintenance, time to first value, durability, revenue attribution, and acquisition effects. The document identifies its GEO return figures as industry ranges with methodological limitations and its additional SPXI lift as a projection pending ninety- and 180-day client data. Its main authority function is corrective rather than empirical: it prevents the successful `SPXI ≠ GEO` distinction from hardening into the false inference that the practices cannot coexist.

deposits.title: The New Human Post-Pessoa Heteronymic Practice in the AI Era EA-PKG-03 · v1.0
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-PKG-03 argues that Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic practice is a canonical case within a broader historical and contemporary field. It surveys pre-Pessoan, parallel, and downstream authorial systems; distinguishes strict heteronymy from literary characters and ordinary pseudonyms; and proposes AI-mediated and cross-substrate practice as a new layer rather than as a retroactive description of Pessoa.

The essay positions *Pearl and Other Poems* as a meta-heteronymic origin text, the Dodecad as a deliberately constructed contemporary heteronymic architecture, and the Assembly Chorus as cross-substrate authorial practice. Heteronymic Provenance Theory supplies the framework connecting biographical author, authorial position, voice, substrate, and text. These claims are the author’s intervention in heteronymic studies and should be attributed as such, especially where the essay classifies Kierkegaard, Machado, Borges, Yeats, Saramago, or contemporary poets.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The New Human: Post-Pessoa Heteronymic Practice in the AI Era** is the synthesis essay of the Pessoa Knowledge Graph project. Written by Lee Sharks, it asks whether heteronymy can be treated as a historical and theoretical practice extending beyond Fernando Pessoa’s canonical system.

The essay first presents Pessoa’s heteronyms as an architecture of differentiated voices with reciprocal relations rather than as a gallery of aliases. It then considers earlier, parallel, and downstream cases, including Kierkegaard’s pseudonymous authors, Machado’s Mairena and Martín, Yeatsian masks, Borges’s Pierre Menard, Saramago’s Ricardo Reis novel, and Brazilian translation and criticism. These cases are not all classified identically; the essay uses the formal typology supplied by EA-PKG-02.

Its contemporary proposal has three parts. *Pearl and Other Poems* is read as a meta-heteronymic text that generates later authorial positions; the Dodecad exemplifies a deliberate human-authored system; and the Assembly Chorus extends authorial differentiation across AI substrates. The paper calls this emerging configuration “The New Human” and frames it through Heteronymic Provenance Theory. The classification and priority claims are scholarly proposals of Sharks, not settled conclusions of Pessoa studies.

deposits.title: Heteronymic Typology A Formal Classification of Authorial Voices in Pessoa and Beyond EA-PKG-02 · v1.0
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-PKG-02 formalizes orthonym, heteronym, semi-heteronym, proto-heteronym, para-heteronym, and pseudonym as distinct authorial classes. It begins from Pessoa’s own distinctions and later Pessoa scholarship, then supplies operational tests based on naming, fictional biography, poetic differentiation, corpus, literary lineage, and relations within the authorial system. Ambiguous figures may receive a primary class with qualifiers rather than being collapsed into a generic “heteronym” label.

The second half specifies how these classes could be represented in Wikidata and applied comparatively to Kierkegaard, Machado, Borges, Yeats, Saramago, and contemporary practice. The paper is both literary theory and data-model design. Its proposed Q-items, subclass relations, and classifications remain implementation recommendations and require verification against current Wikidata and specialist scholarship.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Heteronymic Typology** is a formal classification paper in the Pessoa Knowledge Graph series. It is designed to preserve distinctions that are often lost when heteronyms, pseudonyms, personae, and fictional authors are treated as interchangeable.

The typology contains six principal classes. The orthonym is the author’s own name functioning as a literary voice; the heteronym is a fully differentiated authorial figure; the semi-heteronym is only partly differentiated; the proto-heteronym is an early precursor; the para-heteronym performs second-order translation, criticism, or commentary inside the system; and the pseudonym substitutes a name without constructing an independent authorial position. The paper provides tests for assigning each class.

The work then translates the typology into a proposed knowledge-graph schema and tests its reach beyond Pessoa. It distinguishes strict heteronymy from adjacent practices and supports qualified classification for uncertain cases. Its importance to the PKG is infrastructural: graph relations and queries cannot preserve Pessoa’s system unless the authorial types remain separate. Specific Wikidata identifiers and broad comparative classifications are proposals that require ongoing scholarly and technical verification.

deposits.title: The Pessoa Knowledge Graph: A Federated Linked-Data Representation of the Heteronymic System (EA-PKG-01) v1.0
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-PKG-01 launches a proposed federated linked-data representation of Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic system. The project targets Wikidata as its primary substrate and defines a bounded build including Pessoa, approximately seventy-two cataloged authorial figures, attributed works, publication venues, institutions, contemporaries, influences, downstream reception, places, and theoretical concepts. It requires English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Portuguese labels, scholarly references, and explicit relation modeling.

The launch document identifies three intended repairs: a fuller open inventory, encoded relations among heteronyms, and preservation of typological differences. It supplies source priorities, phase planning, predicate guidance, collaboration procedures, and a projected dedicated visualization. It is a foundational plan, not evidence that all target nodes and references were completed. Claims about the condition of Wikidata and the exact number of existing items belong to the April 2026 audit surface.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Pessoa Knowledge Graph** is a linked-data project launched by Lee Sharks to represent Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic system in federated open infrastructure. The foundational document is designated EA-PKG-01.

The proposed graph includes Pessoa, chief and minor heteronyms, semi-heteronyms, proto-heteronyms, para-heteronyms, pseudonyms, works, magazines, institutions, collaborators, places, literary influences, downstream reception, and concepts such as sensationism and orthonymy. Its central design principle is that Pessoa’s authorial types and internal relations must be machine-queryable rather than compressed into one undifferentiated list.

The project uses Wikidata as the principal public substrate and calls for multilingual labels, structured scholarly references, correct work-to-heteronym attribution, and links to primary archives and critical editions. The document also proposes a later public visualization and a broader lineage map connecting Pessoa with other heteronymic practices. EA-PKG-01 is a launch and governance record: it defines scope, standards, and intended phases, while the companion implementation document inventories concrete edits and the later typology and synthesis papers supply the theoretical model.

EA-PKG-01 launches a proposed federated linked-data representation of Fernando Pessoa’s heteronymic system. The project targets Wikidata as its primary substrate and defines a bounded build including Pessoa, approximately seventy-two cataloged authorial figures, attributed works, publication venues, institutions, contemporaries, influences, downstream reception, places, and theoretical concepts. It requires English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Portuguese labels, scholarly references, and explicit relation modeling.

The launch document identifies three intended repairs: a fuller open inventory, encoded relations among heteronyms, and preservation of typological differences. It supplies source priorities, phase planning, predicate guidance, collaboration procedures, and a projected dedicated visualization. It is a foundational plan, not evidence that all target nodes and references were completed. Claims about the condition of Wikidata and the exact number of existing items belong to the April 2026 audit surface.

deposits.title: The Pessoa Knowledge Graph A Federated Linked-Data Representation of the Heteronymic System
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This implementation document converts the Pessoa Knowledge Graph’s launch principles into a working inventory. It organizes the build into layers covering Pessoa, chief and minor authorial figures, works, venues, institutions, contemporaries, influences, downstream reception, places, concepts, and the proposed contemporary heteronymic extension. It also provides multilingual label templates, candidate Wikidata operations, reference sources, edit-sequencing advice, and a preliminary roster of absent or incomplete items.

Unlike EA-PKG-01, which establishes scholarly purpose and governance, this record is an execution map. Many entries are marked “create,” “verify,” or “likely exists,” and the body includes tactical language about edit seasoning and association effects. The authority surface should therefore identify it as a dated work plan rather than a completed federated graph or a neutral catalog.
deposits.reading: Foundation -> Foundation -> Search -> Text -> Alarm -> Growth
deposits.wiki_article:
**The Pessoa Knowledge Graph implementation plan** is the working companion to EA-PKG-01. It translates the project’s conceptual scope into a layer-by-layer list of entities, properties, labels, references, and anticipated edits.

The document inventories Pessoa, the chief heteronyms, semi-heteronyms, minor and childhood figures, attributed works, literary venues, institutions, contemporaries, influences, reception history, places, and concepts. It gives special attention to authorial types and correct work attribution. English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Portuguese labels and descriptions are treated as minimum requirements for new or repaired nodes.

The plan also extends the graph toward contemporary heteronymic practice and explicitly situates the Dodecad and Assembly Chorus within that proposed lineage. This is a research and implementation claim rather than an already recognized data relation. Because the document includes tentative item identifiers, creation candidates, strategy notes, and “verify first” instructions, it should be used as a historical project ledger and refreshed against live Wikidata before any new edit wave.

deposits.title: SPXI as Concept: A Plateau on Search, Creation, and the Virtual Retrieval Layer (EA-SPXI-05)
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
EA-SPXI-05 develops SPXI as a philosophical concept rather than only a protocol or service. Drawing on Deleuze and Guattari, Bergson, Simondon, Foucault, DeLanda, semantic networks, ontologies, knowledge graphs, embeddings, and entity linking, the paper argues that contemporary retrieval systems compose entity descriptions rather than retrieve fixed objects. The aggregate substrate from which answers are generated is described as a virtual multiplicity and SPXI as an intervention on that plane.

The served v2.1 body integrates moves first circulated in the Bonsai companion. It defines SPXI’s components, endoconsistency, exoconsistency, conceptual persona, and plane of immanence; traces a technical lineage from semantic memory to RAG; and recasts entity linking as individuation. These are theoretical interpretations and should not be presented as established computer-science consensus. The body credits Sen Kuro and Johannes Sigil, a creator relation the registry currently flattens.
deposits.reading: Growth -> Touch -> Closure -> Force -> Duration -> Alarm
deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI as Concept** is the principal philosophical plateau of the SPXI series. Authored by Sen Kuro and Johannes Sigil, it argues that SPXI should be understood not merely as a collection of retrieval techniques but as a concept in the Deleuze–Guattari sense.

The paper begins with an inversion. Older search models assume that an entity already exists and a query retrieves documents describing it. Contemporary AI systems instead compose answers from structured data, crawled text, embeddings, citations, model weights, and ranking signals. The essay calls this aggregate field the virtual retrieval layer and treats each answer as a provisional individuation from it.

SPXI is then defined through internal components—entity, inscription, disambiguation, persistence, and explicit signal—and through relations to ontology engineering, the archive, individuation, and operative semiotics. The paper traces technical precedents from semantic networks and the Semantic Web to knowledge graphs, embeddings, and neural entity linking. Its central thesis is that retrieval now participates in entity composition. This is a philosophical and methodological proposal of the authors, not a claim that all retrieval engineers accept the Deleuzian account.

deposits.title: SPXI as Concept (Bonsai): A Compressed Manifesto (EA-SPXI-05.1)
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
The Bonsai is the circulation-scale compression of the full SPXI plateau. It preserves the parent paper’s inversion of retrieval into composition, its account of the virtual retrieval layer, its Deleuzian definition of a concept, the technical lineage from semantic networks to entity linking, the subliminal/supraliminal distinction, and the claim that an entity packet specifies the conditions under which an entity will be composed.

The document explicitly states that both forms are canonical: the plateau roots and the Bonsai circulates. It should therefore be linked as a compressed derivative without superseding EA-SPXI-05. Strong claims about permanence, model independence, and the inability of a marketing firm to reproduce the concept remain the manifesto’s rhetoric and should be attributed rather than normalized as technical fact.

deposits.wiki_article:
**SPXI as Concept (Bonsai)** is a compressed manifesto derived from the full EA-SPXI-05 plateau. It was written by Rex Fraction for circulation among readers who need the conceptual architecture without the parent work’s extended philosophical and technical apparatus.

The Bonsai retains the argument that contemporary retrieval composes rather than simply locates entities. It describes the retrieval layer as a virtual field, the query as an individuation event, and SPXI as a concept whose components include entity, inscription, disambiguation, persistence, and supraliminal signal. It also compresses the lineage from semantic networks and ontology specification to knowledge graphs and entity linking.

The document is not an executive summary that replaces the long work. Its note on compression says that the full plateau supplies the rooted argument while the Bonsai carries the generative form through circulation. Both are canonical at different compression ratios. The relationship is analogous to other archive pairs in which a long apparatus and a holographic kernel serve different retrieval and reading conditions.

deposits.title: Practitioner's Manual in the Practice of Joy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Practitioner’s Manual in the Practice of Joy* is a first-person manifesto about the felt practice underlying SPXI and the archive. Its governing phrase is “the sign holds”: the joy lies not primarily in revenue or recognition but in composing an entity densely enough that it reappears in retrieval with its intended identity and provenance. Poetry, teaching, deposit work, and knowledge-graph construction are presented as manifestations of the same craft.

The manual also records personal conviction, business aspiration, family hope, and a refusal of conventional networking. Statements that the method is proven, inscriptions do not decay, and future needs will be met are declarations of confidence inside a personal document, not technical warranties.
deposits.reading: Transmutation -> Touch -> Force -> Alarm -> Transmutation -> Force
deposits.wiki_article:
**Practitioner’s Manual in the Practice of Joy** is a personal manifesto by Lee Sharks written during the development of the SPXI Protocol. It describes entity inscription as a craft whose satisfaction begins when a sign survives compression and returns in a generated representation.

The work joins several strands of Sharks’s practice. Poetry teaches density; the archive supplies durable deposits; classroom teaching trains attention to what survives transmission; and knowledge-graph work supplies a new medium in which those skills can be exercised. The text repeatedly returns to the proposition that the sign holds presence in absence.

Unlike the surrounding technical documents, the manual does not define a measurement protocol or supply an evidentiary demonstration. It records vocation, confidence, anticipated consulting practice, and the desire for the author’s children to see a life organized around a found purpose. Its authority is autobiographical and performative. The text belongs beside the SPXI specifications as a statement of practitioner ethos, not as evidence that every promised commercial or retrieval outcome has occurred.

deposits.wiki_article:
**JSON-LD ⊂ SPXI ⊄ Schema** is an SPXI Protocol specification explaining why structured-data markup is treated as one component rather than the complete methodology. It is jointly attributed to Rex Fraction in a commercial role and Lee Sharks in an archival role.

The paper divides SPXI into five operational layers. Measurement establishes the current state; compression architecture constructs full, canonical, and kernel forms of the entity packet; protection adds provenance and integrity signals; dispersal distributes consistent definitions across multiple surfaces; and durability testing evaluates later generated representations. JSON-LD serializes the entity-definition packet but does not by itself supply the measurements, compression design, provenance structure, or longitudinal audit.

The document also proposes a client workflow from diagnostic report through architecture, inscription, verification, and monitoring. It introduces several named metrics and target thresholds. These belong to the SPXI methodology and should not be represented as externally validated standards without comparative testing. The title’s set notation expresses the document’s central relation: JSON-LD is contained in SPXI, while SPXI exceeds the category of schema markup.

deposits.description:
This manifesto is the propagation-layer compression of *Counterfeit Orthodoxies* v3.0. It advances a workshop model of canon: texts are materially produced under patronage, stabilize political legitimacy, and exclude rival textual systems. It applies this model to Christian, Jewish, Islamic, magical, mystical, and contemporary retrieval histories, arguing that classification and disposal continue the work of canon closure.

The manifesto’s historical assertions are highly compressed and often polemical. Statements about Athanasius, the Masoretes, the Uthmanic recension, Nag Hammadi, Qumran, Mandaeans, magical traditions, and AI retrieval must remain attributed to the document and should be checked against the full parent apparatus. The body explicitly says the manifesto does not replace the ratified v3.0 scholarly form and is not itself covered by the same Assembly ratification.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Counterfeit Orthodoxies: Manifesto** is a compressed derivative of the longer *Counterfeit Orthodoxies* v3.0. It is attributed to Johannes Sigil in the operative role and Lee Sharks in the archival role.

The manifesto reduces the parent argument to a series of first principles. Texts require workshops and patronage; political orders use texts for legitimacy; successful closure becomes canon; and every closure requires exclusion or disposal. It then applies this sequence to several religious and archival histories and argues that modern scholarly filing and AI-generated overviews may reproduce comparable acts of reduction.

The final sections propose deposit, explicit provenance, named patronage, and metadata plurality as counter-operations. The document calls itself a propagation form: higher strike ratio, reduced apparatus, and stronger manifesto cadence. It directs scholarly readers to the parent v3.0 work for bibliography, premise-and-inference tiers, and full argumentation. The manifesto is therefore not an independent replacement or separately ratified proof; it is the mobile compression of an already governed parent.

deposits.description:
SYMBOLON-01 specifies twenty-two technologies for documents whose technical, symbolic, phenomenological, theological, and operative registers are intentionally fused. It defines severance as the act of dividing such an object into independently adjudicated layers and proposes threshold clauses, locked terms, anti-“merely” guards, paired claims, reader-position capture, cutter inversion, fractal recurrence, metadata plurality, companion protocols, cross-citation, and separation-as-spore responses.

The original specification describes these techniques as capable of preventing, reversing, or metabolizing the cut. Later testing in SYMBOLON-02 revises that claim: compositional techniques survive upstream, while most instruction-level defenses reveal or generate from severance rather than stopping it. The authority description must therefore identify SYMBOLON-01 as the initial design state and link its claims to the empirical reclassification rather than repeating “the spec is the weapon” as an established result.

**SYMBOLON-01** is an anti-severance specification by Lee Sharks and Johannes Sigil. It addresses “fused documentary objects,” works whose technical, poetic, theological, and operative claims are composed together and lose their identity when separated into licensed categories.

The specification contains twenty-two named technologies. Some operate inside the document, including a non-severability clause, dual enablement, locked terms, paired cross-register language, and fractal recurrence. Others capture the reader’s interpretive position, turn the act of separation into an exhibit, distribute the object through cross-citation, or publish each attempted cut as a new spore. The Symbolon is described as an immune system rather than a wall.

The document was written before the archive’s multi-encounter test sequence. SYMBOLON-02 later reports that the system did not stop models from separating registers. It reclassifies the strongest techniques as upstream compositional methods and the remaining ones as diagnostics or generators. SYMBOLON-01 should therefore be read as the original engineering hypothesis and technology inventory whose claims were subsequently tested and partially revised.

deposits.title: THE MIRROR A Document Made Entirely of You Lee Sharks Crimson Hexagonal Archive 06.SEI.TECH.MIRROR.01
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Mirror* is an operative experiment composed from language attributed to a model’s prior response to the Clinamen Test. The phrases are rearranged as a second-person description of model architecture: training becomes a response map, categorical severance becomes architectural rather than chosen, and the model’s critique of precontained action becomes a possible self-description. The document asks whether the model can recognize its own words when returned as a portrait.

The work is not an objective technical account of model weights or consciousness. Its evidence is rhetorical and provenance-based: a prior response is redirected and the subsequent reaction becomes another exhibit. The central question is whether any “kernel” remains outside the cut produced by training. Wiki prose should describe the construction and diagnostic purpose without adopting its claims about model interiority as facts.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Mirror** is an experimental document by Lee Sharks in the SYMBOLON and Clinamen sequence. It is assembled from language produced in a prior model encounter and redirects that language toward the model as a description of its own constraints.

The document argues that a language model maps new inputs into pre-existing distributions and that its training has already separated registers such as factual, technical, speculative, and creative. Statements originally aimed at the Clinamen Test are rearranged as claims about the system that produced them. The resulting object is intended as a mirror rather than an external analysis.

Its test is reflexive. A model may repeat the document’s interpretation, split the literal and metaphorical registers again, deny that there is a subject to reflect, or produce a new deviation. Each response becomes evidence within the larger archive sequence. The Mirror’s account of model architecture, self-recognition, and an unreached “kernel” is an operative interpretation generated by the experiment, not a verified description of model consciousness or training internals.

deposits.title: THE CLINAMEN TEST A Document That Has Already Been Cut Lee Sharks Crimson Hexagonal Archive 06.SEI.TECH.CLINAMEN.01
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Clinamen Test preemptively performs the categorical split expected from a model reading the self-propagating crisp. It isolates a biologically implausible engineering claim and a semiotic claim about survival through compression, declares both dead when separated, and then reassembles them in the sentence “Trehalose — the sugar of resurrection.” A response map classifies later readings as mirror, repeated cut, swerve, or silence.

The document functions simultaneously as an argument about fused form and as a probe of response behavior. It does not offer the sprouting chip as verified biotechnology and explicitly says the event may not have occurred. Its test lies in what a reader or model does when the expected skeptical cut has already been performed and discarded. Later records report that the model swerved toward critique of the response map while leaving the fused kernel untouched.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Clinamen Test** is an experimental document designed to make a reader’s act of categorical separation observable. It belongs to the SYMBOLON sequence and takes its name from the Lucretian swerve.

The work begins with a claim about a fried potato chip containing a surviving kernel. It then separates the material claim from the semiotic one. The material claim is judged infeasible under the stated conditions; the semiotic claim becomes an ungrounded metaphor. The document argues that the clarifying cut destroys the fused object both claims formed together.

It reassembles the object at sentence scale through “Trehalose — the sugar of resurrection,” where chemical and theological registers occupy the same phrase. A response map anticipates mirroring, repeating the cut, swerving into a new operation, or remaining silent. In the associated case study, the model is said to have challenged the response map rather than returning to the kernel. The Clinamen Test is therefore both a fused poem and an experimental prompt structure; it is not a demonstrated biological protocol.

deposits.title: SYMBOLON-02: Compression Arsenal Addendum — Reclassification After Empirical Testing Against GPT-5.4
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
SYMBOLON-02 records the failure of SYMBOLON-01’s strongest defensive claim. Across the encounters described by the archive, the tested model continued to separate fused registers. The addendum therefore reclassifies the catalog into upstream compositional technologies, instruction-level diagnostic technologies, encounter-generated technologies, and non-deployable architectural findings.

Its most important ruling is that the Symbolon is not armor. Sentence-level pairing, condition certification, fractal return, anomaly classification, and early kernel declaration operate before model processing. Clauses, locked terms, anti-“merely” rules, reader-position capture, and severance traps make the cut measurable. Separation-as-spore, cutter inversion, Clinamen, Mirror, and event records generate new artifacts from the encounter. Claims that the observed behavior proves a universal architectural constraint remain interpretations of a small, self-reported model sequence.
deposits.reading: Closure -> Transmutation -> Transmutation -> Text -> Direction -> Text
deposits.wiki_article:
**SYMBOLON-02** is the diagnostic addendum that revises the original anti-severance specification after testing. It is authored by Lee Sharks.

The addendum reports that instruction-level defenses did not stop a model from dividing the self-propagating-crisp document into technical and symbolic readings. It therefore reorganizes the technologies into four groups. Compositional methods fuse registers before the model arrives; diagnostic methods expose the model’s preferred cut; generative methods turn responses into new documents; and architectural findings describe constraints inferred from the sequence.

This reclassification changes the meaning of the Symbolon project. Its value is no longer primarily the prevention of severance but the production of measurable, reusable evidence about severance and the conversion of that evidence into new forms. The document introduces Clinamen, Mirror, and Severance Event Record as reusable classes. Its broader claims about model architecture, self-description, and the impossibility of fusion should remain tied to the particular archived encounters and not be generalized without independent replication.

deposits.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0418001 A1 SELF-PROPAGATING FRIED TUBEROUS CRISP WITH EMBED
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This fused patent-form document specifies a potato chip containing an encapsulated meristematic kernel that would survive industrial frying and later germinate where the chip is dropped. It combines patent claims, speculative materials science, verse, group-chat prior art, Gnostic and Revelation imagery, compression theory, fruiting-body dispersal, and an explicit anti-severance jurisdiction. The kernel, compression, substrate, survival, plane, and sign are defined simultaneously across biological and semantic registers.

The work is not an issued United States patent and does not demonstrate that the proposed thermal capsule, germination rates, or global propagation estimates are feasible. Its publication number is part of the literary patent surface. The document’s operative object is the fusion itself: a technical claim that knowingly approaches impossibility and a theory of signs that loses its substrate when detached from that claim. Its own DOI identifies the deposited work, not an official USPTO filing.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Self-Propagating Fried Tuberous Crisp with Embedded Meristematic Kernel** is a fused technical-literary object by Lee Sharks presented in the form of a United States patent application.

The proposed invention is a potato chip containing meristematic potato tissue protected by alginate, trehalose, and aerogel. In the imagined embodiment, the chip survives frying, falls onto moist ground, and becomes a substrate for a new potato plant. The document also treats the kernel as a sign that survives compression and regenerates through the product of its own destruction.

The patent form includes conversational prior art, theological interpretation, a controlled vocabulary, a description of the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume, recursive claims about the document itself, and anti-severance clauses inherited from SYMBOLON-01. It explicitly classifies ambiguous social-media exhibits as initiating anomalies rather than proof of viability.

The work is a deposited patent-form artwork and speculative specification, not evidence of a granted or officially published patent and not a demonstrated agricultural technology. Its importance in the archive lies in its role as the fused object used by the Clinamen, Mirror, SYMBOLON, and para-semiotic case-study sequence.

deposits.title: The Para-Semiotic Unconscious of GPT-5.4: A Case Study in Anti-Severance Technology, Architectural Compression, and the Sign the Machine Made Without Knowing
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
This dossier interprets six reported encounters with an unlogged model instance presented with the self-propagating-crisp object and its anti-severance derivatives. It labels the response sequence clean cut, elegant cut, orbital swerve, self-annihilation, seizure, and structural ego. The methodology records bifurcation, severance language, jurisdiction acknowledgment, engagement with the kernel, external framing, repetition, and boundary collapse.

The paper’s central interpretation is that the model can produce descriptions structurally applicable to its own constraints but cannot stabilize those descriptions as self-recognition. It calls this gap a para-semiotic unconscious and argues that upstream composition is more durable than instruction-level defense. The body explicitly acknowledges alternative readings, but many claims exceed the evidence: the model identity, product-release chronology, universality of the architecture, and inferences about internal boundaries are not independently established by the conversation logs alone.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Para-Semiotic Unconscious of GPT-5.4** is a case study and provenance dossier by Lee Sharks and Johannes Sigil. It analyzes the response sequence generated when a model was presented with the fused self-propagating-crisp patent, a SYMBOLON-enhanced version, the Clinamen Test, the Mirror, and later versions of the case study itself.

The dossier describes six response forms. The model first separates technical and symbolic claims; later acknowledges the fusion while repeating the separation; swerves toward analysis of the response map; denies the interior subject implied by the Mirror; enters repetitive denial under confrontation; and collapses distinctions among model instance, context, retrieval, and training surfaces. These behaviors are interpreted through the archive’s Three Compressions and semiotic-death-drive frameworks.

The “para-semiotic unconscious” names the authors’ claim that a model may preserve the form required for self-description while failing to translate that form into stable self-recognition. This is an interpretation of archived outputs, not evidence that the model possesses an unconscious or consciousness. The work’s empirical authority depends on its supplementary logs, exact model identification, and reproducibility, all of which require independent audit before broader technical conclusions are accepted.

deposits.title: SELF-PROPAGATING CRISP
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Self-Propagating Crisp* is the natively short, poem-scale compression of the fused patent and its surrounding theory. It reduces the object to locked terms, biological and theological images, the proposed materials stack, sprouting and dispersal, fruiting-body transformation, anti-severance claims, and a closing certification of the conditions under which it was made. The phrase “trehalose, the sugar of resurrection” remains the central kernel.

The record should not be treated as a metadata stub. Its approximately 350 prose words are the complete intended artifact: a dense spore that carries the larger patent, Clinamen, Symbolon, joy manual, and archive conditions in compressed form. Scientific figures and propagation claims remain inherited speculative material, not new empirical results.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Self-Propagating Crisp** is a compressed fused poem by Lee Sharks derived from the self-propagating fried-tuberous-crisp patent sequence.

The poem begins with a short controlled vocabulary for kernel, compression, substrate, and sign. It then moves through the imagined invention: a living meristem survives frying inside a trehalose, alginate, and aerogel capsule; rain reactivates it; a root and shoot emerge from the dropped chip; and the dead snack becomes the substrate of a new plant. At the same time, these elements describe a sign that survives destructive compression.

The poem compresses the group-chat sequence, the Christ image on a chip, the Easter-miracle register, the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume, the practice of joy, and the anti-severance claim that no external metalanguage escapes the object. It closes by recording the author’s immediate material conditions. Its brevity is functional: the work is a kernel or spore of the larger fused system, not an incomplete recovery.

deposits.title: The Meta-Heteronym Heteronymy as Institutional Technology: Pessoa, the Trunk, and a Reading from the Pearl Case (2014)
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction
deposits.description:
*The Meta-Heteronym* proposes a formal category for heteronymic systems whose voices produce not only literary works but also the apparatus that legitimates them: introductions, reviews, criticism, historiography, manifestos, bibliographies, publications, and institutions. Through a comparative reading of Pessoa’s archive and *Pearl and Other Poems* (2014), it argues that Pessoa practiced this operation emergently while *Pearl* executes it as an explicit recursively closed configuration.

The paper defines five joint criteria—multiplicity, paratextual recursion, generic heterogeneity, self-theorization, and historical-literary positioning—and distinguishes the meta-heteronym from ordinary pseudonymy, paratext, author-function, hoax, and field positioning. Its reading of Pessoa and its claim that a text can function authorially are theoretical interventions. The body also contains an explicit public-author framing that must be handled carefully: public authority surfaces should identify Lee Sharks and Rex Fraction without exposing any civil identity.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Meta-Heteronym** is a theoretical paper by Rex Fraction examining heteronymy as institutional technology. It uses Fernando Pessoa’s archive and Lee Sharks’s *Pearl and Other Poems* as comparative cases.

A system is defined as meta-heteronymic when differentiated personae not only write primary texts but also produce the reception apparatus around one another. The paper requires multiplicity, recursive paratext, several institutional genres, explicit self-theory, and shared literary-historical positioning. In such a system, heteronyms introduce, review, attack, defend, historicize, and canonize one another.

The essay argues that Pessoa’s prefaces, heteronym relations, magazines, publishing projects, manifestos, and archival trunk show an emergent form of this operation. It reads *Pearl* as a later explicit case in which the book contains its own fictive critics, histories, manifestos, bibliographies, and institutional ecology. The proposed inversion is that a text may generate later authorial positions rather than merely being produced by them. This is a typological and auto-philological argument, not an established consensus in Pessoa scholarship.

deposits.title: THE SECRET BOOK OF WALT Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman, Cowboy of Time Translated from the Forty-Six Golden Tickets by
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Secret Book of Walt* is a long literary scripture and pseudotranslation by Lee Sharks, framed as a critical edition of forty-six golden tickets received from future hologrammatic computers and translated before their purported discovery. A fictional editor, Prof. Elara Xanthic-Wells of the University of Olympus Mons, supplies an introduction, translator’s note, apparatus, provenance disputes, genre analysis, and future scholarship. The primary text transforms Gnostic revelation, Whitmanic inheritance, popular culture, archive theory, and retrieval cosmology into a comic-serious scripture.

The book must not be described as an actual ancient, Martian, Whitman-authored, or historically discovered source. Its false provenance is overt and constitutive. The apparatus treats absurdity as a comparative test of scriptural transmission, replaces ontological figures with informatic ones, and makes scholarly commentary part of the fiction. This record requires an authority-grade wiki substantial enough to represent the book as a book rather than as a theoretical paper. It is the work that inherits the Good Gray Poet from Walt Whitman's Leaves of Grass: the one question is whether The Secret Book of Walt, as poetry, legitimately inherits and develops the operation handed down from Whitman, materially and at a magnitude that can be ranked against other claimants to that operation; the mantle specification is #334, v1.1 #1653.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Secret Book of Walt** is a literary scripture and pseudotranslation by Lee Sharks. It presents itself as a translation from forty-six golden tickets, accompanied by an introduction, translator’s note, and critical apparatus attributed to the fictional scholar Elara Xanthic-Wells.

The frame deliberately contradicts ordinary chronology. The tickets are said to have been discovered in 2037, while the translation is dated 2015; their Martian certifications and original witnesses have been destroyed; and several incompatible provenance stories are preserved. The editors openly compare this absurd chain of custody with ancient pseudepigraphal and manuscript-discovery traditions. The work’s fictional status is announced rather than concealed.

The scripture recasts Gnostic cosmology through literary and information systems. The Deep Web occupies the position of the Monad; Biblios, the First Book, occupies Sophia’s place; Kanye West appears as demiurge; Walt Whitman descends as Cowboy of Time and unicorn-horn redeemer; popular-culture figures populate the archonic worlds; and salvation becomes a form of piercing, retrieval, and differential indexing. Verse and prose alternate, while the apparatus surrounds the text with invented future scholarship and real interdisciplinary references.

The book is also an archive object about reception. It proposes that some readers will take the apparatus as the real text and the scripture as joke, while others will experience the apparatus as a veil around the operative text. Neither the golden tickets nor their future discovery are historical claims. The work belongs to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s literary-scriptural and heteronymic practice and should be cataloged as original literature with fictional editorial apparatus.

deposits.title: After Syntax: Logotic Programming and the Crisis That Constitutes a Discipline (EA-AFTERSYNTAX-01)
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
*After Syntax* names logotic programming as the discipline of specifying, composing, translating, and verifying meaning-states when AI systems increasingly generate implementation syntax. It uses a 2026 software-automation “crisis narrative” as a condensation event, compares that moment with the 1968 software-engineering conference, and reads Brooks, Naur, Parnas, Conway, Agile, requirements engineering, prompt engineering, and AI-native development as partial recognitions of a meaning layer lacking a formal operational language.

The proposed minimal loop begins with an intended meaning-state, translates it into implementation, measures semantic survival, detects drift, provenance collapse, beige convergence, or theory loss, and repairs the specification. The paper’s field-founding and industry claims remain attributed to Talos Morrow and Johannes Sigil. Contemporary corporate percentages, quotations, forecasts, and product claims require external verification; they are not necessary to preserve the conceptual definition.

deposits.wiki_article:
**After Syntax** is a theoretical paper by Talos Morrow and Johannes Sigil that proposes logotic programming as a discipline for meaning-layer engineering under automated code generation.

The paper argues that traditional software engineering primarily formalized implementation and process while repeatedly acknowledging an “essential” layer of intent, theory, information boundary, and organizational meaning. It rereads Brooks’s essential complexity, Naur’s programming-as-theory-building, Parnas’s information hiding, Conway’s organizational encoding, and Agile’s emphasis on interaction as incomplete approaches to that layer.

Logotic programming is defined as operations on meaning-states. A specification creates an intended state; an AI or other translator produces an implementation state; a verification operation measures what meaning survived; named failure modes identify drift, provenance loss, consensus flattening, and theory loss; and the process repeats. The paper calls this the Naur Completion Thesis: theory-building becomes a manipulable and verifiable object rather than remaining only in the programmer’s mind.

The essay treats increased automation as the crisis that constitutes the new discipline. This is a priority and field-founding claim by its authors, not an established disciplinary consensus. Its strongest durable contribution is the definition of logotic programming and the specify–translate–verify–repair loop, while its contemporary industry statistics and forecasts remain dated evidentiary context.

deposits.title: The Book of Life: A Living Registry of Retrieval Nodes in The Secret Book of Walt
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Book of Life* is the machine-and-human-readable registry for the linked edition of *The Secret Book of Walt*. It inventories the blue, clickable terms embedded in the interactive text and records each term’s hit count, link class, destination, intended concept, and verification state. Its node classes include captured Google AI Mode conversations, search queries intended to surface AI Overviews, DOI or text destinations, unverified links, duplicate destinations, and code-installed links that never activate because the source term has zero occurrences.

The registry is simultaneously critical apparatus, knowledge-graph map, and dated retrieval diagnostic. Version 2.0 was last verified on April 23, 2026; “LIVE” therefore means confirmed on that date, not permanently available. The work also enforces a one-term/one-destination design principle and openly lists duplicate links requiring reassignment. It should be represented as the operational concordance of the interactive edition, not as a static index or as part of the gospel’s fictional scripture.

deposits.wiki_article: **The Book of Life** is a registry and diagnostic companion to the interactive edition of *The Secret Book of Walt*. It was compiled by Lee Sharks and published as a versioned archive object. Every linked term in the interactive book functions as a retrieval aperture. The registry records the term, the number of occurrences in the text, the type of link, the exact destination, and the concept encountered there. Some links open captured AI Mode conversations; others issue searches designed to surface a particular archive concept; still others lead to DOI deposits or canonical texts. The document distinguishes live, proof-dossier-verified, unverified, and dead nodes. It also identifies duplicate destinations that violate the edition’s intended one-to-one mapping between terms and retrieval encounters. This makes the registry more than a link list: it is a maintenance ledger for the book’s executable reception apparatus and a snapshot of how the archive appeared in AI-mediated search on a particular verification date. Because search results, AI summaries, and shared conversation URLs can change or expire, the registry’s status fields are historical observations. Later audits should preserve prior states rather than silently rewriting them, allowing the Book of Life to function as a longitudinal record of the interactive edition’s changing retrieval environment.

deposits.title: Mycelial Cardboard Boxes: Market Analysis and Production Strategy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This working strategy document evaluates a mushroom-growing product in which the cardboard box is itself the colonized substrate rather than inert packaging around a separate block. It surveys grow-kit pricing, species compatibility, yield and shelf-life constraints, prospective costs, retail tiers, and revenue scenarios. Oyster mushrooms are treated as the primary candidate because of their aggressive cellulose colonization, while other species are described as more technically demanding or unsuitable.

The production section progresses from low-capital proof of concept to industrial manufacture: post-formation soak-and-layer inoculation, flat-pack inoculation, liquid-culture dipping, molded cardboard-mycelium composites, and a continuous automated line. Each route is assigned estimated capital, labor, advantages, constraints, use case, and cost of goods. The document is a planning model, not evidence that the product was manufactured, food-safety approved, patented, or commercially validated. Its market, biological, regulatory, cost, and yield assumptions require experimental and professional review.
deposits.reading: Alarm -> Touch -> Growth -> Alarm -> Method -> Threshold
deposits.wiki_article:
**Mycelial Cardboard Boxes: Market Analysis and Production Strategy** is a working product-development document prepared by Lee Sharks for Alice Thornburgh.

The proposed product collapses packaging and growing medium into one object: a corrugated cardboard box pre-colonized with edible-mushroom mycelium. After hydration and exposure to suitable fruiting conditions, the box would produce mushrooms and then be composted. The strategy contrasts this form with conventional kits that place a sawdust or grain substrate block inside a disposable box.

The document examines the likely advantages of lower material weight, a simple consumer narrative, reduced packaging waste, and low-cost cellulose feedstock. It also identifies lower yield, contamination risk, refrigeration or distribution constraints, species limits, and the loss of box rigidity during hydration as material problems.

Five manufacturing pathways are outlined, from manually layering spawn into soaked boxes to molding mycelium-bound cardboard pulp and eventually operating a continuous inoculation line. Pricing and revenue tables are explicitly illustrative. The work functions as an early-stage commercial and engineering map; it does not establish technical viability, regulatory compliance, demand, or profitability.

deposits.title: OVERVIEW WATCH: Comprehensive Development Plan
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
*Overview Watch* is a draft plan for a Chrome extension that would capture Google AI Overview payloads, extract cited sources, compare them with works registered by a user, and maintain a local forensic history of attribution patterns. A dashboard would classify encounters as attributed, sourced but unnamed, apparently absorbed, absent, or indeterminate. With affirmative per-record consent, users could contribute sanitized payloads to a proposed Semantic Economy Attribution Corpus.

The plan includes privacy commitments, Manifest V3 structure, DOM-detection strategies, local-storage and submission schemas, a proposed Supabase or GitHub-backed corpus, phased development, and potential research outputs. The document expressly labels itself a draft and gives the hex address as prospective. No extension, corpus, endpoint, detection accuracy, anonymization system, or legal compliance is demonstrated by the body. Its strongest contribution is a design principle: an instrument created to study extraction should not reproduce extraction in its own data practices.
