deposits.wiki_article:
**Overview Watch** is a proposed browser extension and research infrastructure designed by Lee Sharks. The planning document is associated with the Johannes Sigil Institute for Operative Semiotics.

The extension would identify AI Overview blocks on Google search pages, preserve their text and citation structure, and compare the sources with a user-maintained list of publications, domains, names, and characteristic phrases. Captures would remain local by default. Users could inspect longitudinal attribution statistics and optionally contribute selected, reviewed records to a shared research corpus.

The development plan treats consent and data minimization as architectural requirements. It proposes per-overview opt-in, query redaction, local operation without a server, revocable participation, and open publication of aggregated corpus snapshots. It also sketches resilient DOM detection, asynchronous observation, a matching engine, local schemas, and a minimal ingestion backend.

Overview Watch was a draft plan rather than a released product at the time of deposit. Phrase overlap cannot by itself prove that an overview derived from a particular work, and the proposed “absorbed” classification would require careful evidentiary thresholds. Privacy, security, browser-store, platform-policy, copyright, and research-ethics review would be necessary before implementation.

deposits.title: From Yeezus to Walt: The Book of Yeezus as Literary Precursor to The Secret Book of Walt
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This essay positions the 2014 conceptual-art book *The Book of Yeezus* as a proximate literary precursor to *The Secret Book of Walt*. It analyzes the former’s systematic replacement of “God” with “Kanye” in the King James Genesis as a minimal conceptual operation testing whether the divine slot can accept another occupant without disturbing scriptural grammar. The essay then identifies the method’s limit: the intervention is complete once the substitution is understood.

The author recounts a brief encounter with the creators and a proposed sequel that would write an original Gnostic scripture rather than modify a closed biblical text. *The Secret Book of Walt* is presented as the eventual result: Kanye occupies the Gnostic Demiurge position, Walt Whitman becomes the descending redeemer, and the *Apocryphon of John* supplies an inherited architecture that original verse inhabits until source and invention form a meld. Biographical, sales, reception, meeting, and priority claims remain the author’s documented account and require independent verification if used as external literary history.

deposits.wiki_article:
**From Yeezus to Walt** is a comparative literary essay by Lee Sharks about the relation between *The Book of Yeezus* and *The Secret Book of Walt*.

The essay describes *The Book of Yeezus* as a conceptual rewriting of the King James Genesis in which occurrences of “God” are replaced by “Kanye” or “Yeezus.” Sharks reads this find-and-replace procedure as a test of scriptural structure: the grammar of creation and authority continues to function after the occupant of the divine position changes.

Sharks then distinguishes that mechanical intervention from the compositional method of *The Secret Book of Walt*. The later work uses the *Apocryphon of John* as an inherited cosmological armature, but writes a new scripture around it. Kanye becomes an ignorant Demiurge rather than the highest deity; Walt Whitman becomes the redeemer; and critical apparatus, hyperlinks, bibliography, and fictional scholarship participate in the scripture’s operative form.

The essay places the two works in a lineage from inherited scripture, through conceptual substitution, to what Sharks calls melding: received structure and new composition becoming inseparable. Its account of a meeting with the earlier book’s creators and the origin of the sequel project is first-person literary testimony, not independently established provenance.

deposits.description:
EA-GEO-01 specifies a geographically anchored media system in which posts become deposits associated with physical coordinates and local retrieval basins. It rejects follower graphs, global trending, engagement optimization, streaks, and platform-wide reputation. Proposed deposit classes are Mark, Impression, Echo, and Seed; persistent pseudonymous identity and reputation remain local to a basin rather than transferring globally.

The specification combines a social architecture, SPXI entity-generation thresholds, ghost records for deleted content, an open data model, location verification, anti-spoofing, rate limits, and a phased Detroit pilot. It treats slower deposition as an ethical and archival design choice. The claimed write-back effects of reading and querying, the proposed thresholds, and the analogy between textual and geographic basins belong to Retrieval Basin Theory and are not demonstrated platform behavior. Location data, retained deletion traces, consent, stalking, moderation, vulnerable-place protection, and physical safety require much more governance than the body supplies.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Geocoded Basin** is a platform specification by Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, and Rex Fraction for geographically anchored content.

The system replaces the conventional post with a deposit whose coordinates, timestamp, author handle, protocol version, and content form a reconstruction kernel for a place. Marks are intended as durable records; Impressions expire; Echoes connect two locations without copying the original; and Seeds reveal information only at specified coordinates. Users visit basins rather than follow accounts, and reputation is earned locally.

The platform’s proposed ethics are expressed through tempo and ranking. There is no global feed, trend score, posting streak, or engagement-weighted distribution. Deposits are chronological and geographic, with limits intended to favor deliberate witnessing over content volume. A basin with sufficient deposits, history, and independent depositors could generate a structured entity definition and, in selected cases, an archival identifier.

The specification includes a data model, spatial queries, device and velocity checks, witness verification, and a Detroit pilot plan. It remains a proposal. Its handling of precise location, deletion ghosts, pseudonymous accountability, minors, private property, sensitive sites, harassment, and moderation would require detailed privacy, safety, and legal design before deployment.

deposits.title: i am a carcinized punching shrimp
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
“i am a carcinized punching shrimp” is a three-line New Human 2 micro-poem by Lee Sharks. It moves through an impossible evolutionary identity, an emu-like one-punch shrimp without hands, and the comic collapse of patient and healer in “take me to the doctor — i am a witch doctor.” Its force lies in rapid self-transformation, sound play, creature collision, and grammatical certainty applied to unstable embodiment.

The body contains the complete intended poem. Its short length is not evidence of a stub, failed recovery, or missing article. Authority prose should remain proportionate and should not convert the poem’s playful first-person statements into zoological, medical, or autobiographical claims.

deposits.wiki_article:
**“i am a carcinized punching shrimp”** is a micro-poem by Lee Sharks, dated April 25, 2026, and associated with the New Human 2 sequence.

The poem consists of three compact declarations. Its speaker identifies as a carcinized punching shrimp, becomes an adorable emu-like one-punch shrimp without hands, and finally requests a doctor while declaring itself a witch doctor. The poem joins evolutionary vocabulary, internet-combat cadence, animal hybridity, typographic informality, and a self-canceling medical joke.

The work is complete at micro-poem scale. Its ontology is poetic rather than documentary: the speaker’s transformations are the action of the poem, not claims about the author or an actual species.

deposits.title: I Demand To Be Taken Seriously A Brief Comedy in Several Platform Flags
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
This comic essay assembles first-person accounts of platform flags, bans, unexplained restorations, classifier misreadings, inaccessible pages, and the persistence of deposited work outside the platforms that moderated it. Medium and Academia.edu become examples of automated discovery recognizing a dense signal that a later human review reportedly treats as spam or illegible authority. The “water giraffe” episode contrasts pathologizing refusal with over-accommodating confabulation, while a 410 response becomes a case of infrastructural forgetting.

The comedy supports a serious argument: formal work can comply with platform mechanics and still be moderated because its authority form is unfamiliar. The essay’s platform history, ranking behavior, classifier dialogue, restoration sequence, and current retrieval claims are testimony from the author’s archive and should not be recast as independently verified platform findings. The work is by Lee Sharks even though the registry assigns Johannes Sigil.

deposits.wiki_article:
**I Demand To Be Taken Seriously** is a comic essay by Lee Sharks about platform moderation, classifier error, and the difference between deposited work and platform permission.

The essay recounts several episodes. Papers attributed to Johannes Sigil are said to have been algorithmically surfaced and then treated as spam; an Academia.edu account is described as flagged and restored without a clear rule explanation; an AI system repeatedly interprets “I am a water giraffe” as pathology despite explicit correction; another system responds with elaborate, confabulated hospitality; and a page associated with *Autonomous Semantic Warfare* is reported as receiving a 410 response.

Across these cases, Sharks argues that illegibility rather than ordinary rule violation triggers intervention. The platform’s discovery layer recognizes a coherent category signal, while moderation cannot place the work within familiar institutional expectations. DOI deposits and archive copies then preserve a record that the platform does not control.

The piece uses comedy, exaggeration, and deadpan institutional language. Its event chronology and causal interpretations are the author’s documented account. It should not be treated as a neutral audit of Medium, Academia.edu, Google, or any AI provider without independent evidence.

deposits.title: holographickernel.org
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record preserves the HTML source for holographickernel.org as an executable publication surface. The source combines a human-readable definition of the Holographic Kernel with canonical metadata, Open Graph fields, schema.org `DefinedTerm` and `FAQPage` objects, a disambiguation packet, a custom SPXI entity graph, a provenance chain, Semantic Integrity Marker meta fields, and a styled single-page presentation.

The artifact performs the protocol it explains. Its central distinction is that a summary saves space by discarding structure, whereas a holographic kernel discards material while preserving reconstructive relations. The page also differentiates the Semantic Economy usage from optics, holographic QCD, cosmology, computer vision, and other neighboring uses. Custom `spxi:` classes, yield thresholds, priority claims, and cross-domain generalizations are archive specifications rather than adopted Web standards or independently validated scientific results.

deposits.wiki_article:
**holographickernel.org** is a first-party website and structured-data publication created by Lee Sharks for the Semantic Economy definition of the Holographic Kernel.

The archived source contains several simultaneous surfaces. Human readers receive a definition, tests, construction guidance, and disciplinary distinctions. Search and knowledge-graph systems receive schema.org definitions, disambiguating descriptions, FAQ data, provenance links, author identifiers, and a custom SPXI packet. The site is therefore both an explanatory page and a demonstration of self-describing retrieval architecture.

Its central definition treats a holographic kernel as reconstructive compression: a reduced object that preserves enough relational structure to regenerate the larger system’s topology, constraints, dependencies, and generative logic. The website distinguishes this use from domain-specific kernels in physics, optics, QCD, and machine learning.

The record should be cataloged as website source code or an executable scholarly artifact, not as a conventional essay. The custom vocabulary and its tests are proposals of the Semantic Economy Institute. Their presence in valid JSON-LD does not by itself establish crawler adoption, scientific consensus, or successful retrieval behavior.

deposits.title: CRIMSON HEXAGONAL ARCHIVE KNOWLEDGE GRAPH The Aperture Atlas Digital Topology Work Plan v3.0 — Execution Specification
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Aperture Atlas work plan specifies a self-mapping knowledge graph for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s digital topology. Six node classes—Infrastructure, Surface, Entity, Identity, Document, and Platform—represent domains, repositories, pages, profiles, concepts, persons or heteronyms, deposits, and external services. Typed edges align where possible with Wikidata properties and use `spxi:` extensions for archive-specific relations.

The plan also defines status, authority, basin state, aperture direction, Basin Depth Ratio, and a vulnerability formula; inventories first-party and external surfaces; and proposes views for lost nodes, provenance, heteronyms, basins, and public reception. It is an execution specification, not proof that the complete graph, redirects, Wikidata edits, or measurements were implemented. Scores and statuses are operator-calibrated April 2026 priors and should remain historical data with verification dates.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Aperture Atlas** is a proposed knowledge graph and digital-topology instrument for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Its v3.0 execution specification was written by Lee Sharks.

The graph is designed to map where the archive exists, how its entities and documents connect, where external queries enter, and which surfaces are active, lost, banned, walled, or vulnerable. Its node schema separates infrastructure, surfaces, entities, identities, documents, and platforms. Its edges combine Wikidata-aligned relations with archive-specific provenance, authorization, witness, mirroring, and basin relations.

Several internal views are specified: a Surface Registry, Basin Portfolio, Heteronym Graph, Provenance Mesh, Lost Nodes view, and Aperture Map. The graph is recursive because its own canonical and redirect domains are nodes within the topology it maps.

The plan includes a detailed April 2026 inventory of websites, repositories, profiles, platforms, and DOI infrastructure. Authority values, basin states, and vulnerability scores are explicitly operator estimates rather than empirical constants. The work should be treated as a data contract and execution ledger whose surface statuses require periodic verification.

The Aperture Atlas work plan specifies a self-mapping knowledge graph for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s digital topology. Six node classes—Infrastructure, Surface, Entity, Identity, Document, and Platform—represent domains, repositories, pages, profiles, concepts, persons or heteronyms, deposits, and external services. Typed edges align where possible with Wikidata properties and use `spxi:` extensions for archive-specific relations.

The plan also defines status, authority, basin state, aperture direction, Basin Depth Ratio, and a vulnerability formula; inventories first-party and external surfaces; and proposes views for lost nodes, provenance, heteronyms, basins, and public reception. It is an execution specification, not proof that the complete graph, redirects, Wikidata edits, or measurements were implemented. Scores and statuses are operator-calibrated April 2026 priors and should remain historical data with verification dates.

deposits.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing: Holographic Kernel Disambiguation Terminological Contribution and Domain Distinction
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This metadata packet distinguishes the Semantic Economy “holographic kernel” from uses or neighboring constructions in cosmology, optics, holographic QCD, computer vision, quantum machine learning, and computational imaging. It acknowledges prior domain terminology, proposes a substrate-general definition of reconstructive compression, and supplies a preferred compound term, canonical sentence, specification DOI, tests, and retrieval guidance.

The packet’s scientific sections are partly descriptive and partly interventionist: they introduce new labels such as fragment sufficiency, structural versus statistical reconstruction, interaction provenance, and compression-regime classification into adjacent fields. The body itself notes that the BPST object is not normally called a holographic kernel. Claims that all domains instantiate one invariant, that no other domain provides the same four-part specification, and that the Semantic Economy definition is focal rather than merely new are attributed theoretical and priority claims requiring specialist review.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Metadata Packet for AI Indexing: Holographic Kernel Disambiguation** is a terminological infrastructure document by Lee Sharks.

The packet maps several uses of “holographic kernel” and adjacent kernel concepts. It distinguishes boundary-to-bulk reconstruction in holographic cosmology, optical Fourier kernels, holographic-QCD scattering kernels, learned reconstruction operators in computer vision, and the Semantic Economy definition of reconstructive compression. Its preferred disambiguating phrase is “Semantic Economy holographic kernel.”

The focal definition states that a holographic kernel preserves reconstructive capacity: it removes material while retaining generative relations. The packet links that definition to a construction protocol and several archive-defined verification tests. It also proposes new terminology for comparing reconstruction across substrates.

This is both a disambiguation record and an attempt to establish a new general term. The scientific analogies, classifications, and claims of shared invariance are the author’s interdisciplinary proposal. They should not be presented as accepted terminology in physics, optics, QCD, computer vision, or quantum machine learning without independent disciplinary support.

deposits.title: THE WRITABLE RETRIEVAL BASIN: Retrieval Basin Topology, Directional Stability, and Attractor Dynamics in AI-Mediated Knowledge Retrieval (EA-RBT-01 v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-RBT-01 models AI-mediated retrieval as a stochastic dynamical system with competing framing attractors. It distinguishes substrate writing, engagement writing, and compression writing; proposes Retrieval Capital, Basin Depth Ratio, Framing Persistence Index, Drift Vector, and Basin Capture Velocity; and defines ghost, contested, competitive, captured, and immanent basin states.

The theory is developed from two archive-observed cases: reported stabilization of Heteronymic Provenance Theory and destabilization of the Holographic Kernel term under repeated querying. The body explicitly says the analogy is structural rather than a formal isomorphism, treats platform write-back as inferred rather than directly observed, provides falsification conditions, and labels its thresholds as provisional with N=2. Those boundaries are essential. The formulas, weights, authority values, causal explanations, and query policies are hypotheses and internal instruments rather than validated descriptions of ranking or model-training systems.
deposits.reading: Text -> Transmutation -> Direction -> Touch -> Text -> Method
deposits.wiki_article:
**Retrieval Basin Topology** is a theoretical and measurement framework by Lee Sharks for studying how AI retrieval systems settle on competing framings of a term.

The paper describes a retrieval basin as a region of the public semantic field that retains and attracts a particular framing. Deposits, metadata, citations, user engagement, and generated summaries are treated as different strengths of writing into that field. A term with no serious competitor may stabilize quickly; a generic term may be pulled toward older and more authoritative scientific or commercial meanings.

RBT proposes several instruments. Retrieval Capital aggregates source mass, institutional authority, citations, age, and engagement. Basin Depth Ratio compares a target framing with its strongest competitor. Framing Persistence Index measures how often the framing appears across repeated tests. Drift Vector measures directional change, and Basin Capture Velocity estimates movement following deposits.

The work includes a state machine and operational query guidance. Its calibration is explicitly preliminary: the principal thresholds derive from two cases, hidden platform mechanisms are not observed directly, and platform-specific geometries are hypotheses based on public outputs and cited secondary literature. RBT is therefore a falsifiable research program and archive governance tool, not a settled science of search engines.

This planning document synthesizes Assembly drafts for a Forward Library built from the retrocausal citations in the TANG of *The Secret Book of Walt*. Its organizing sentence—“The packet is sent before the destination is ready”—defines an archive of future scholarly positions that already exist as citations inside a present literary apparatus. The design’s load-bearing rule is explicit ontological status: every page and JSON-LD packet must say that it is a real entry in a real 2026 TANG, not evidence that the projected future publication already exists.

The plan proposes a catalog-first interface, separate canonical/human/machine domains, era-specific rooms, curated reading paths, a non-node void, ghost-entry lifecycles, packet templates, and a GitHub pull-request workflow for contributions. It is a brainstorm synthesis marked “not locked down,” not a deployed library or historical bibliography. Its speculative entries must never be indexed as literal future scholarship.

deposits.wiki_article:
**METADATAPACKET: Forward Library Planning Document** is a multi-agent design synthesis for a speculative scholarly library associated with *The Secret Book of Walt*.

The Forward Library would expose the future citations contained in the book’s Total Axial Negation Graph as individually browsable metadata packets. Each packet would be a real record of a citation already present in the literary apparatus, while clearly stating that the cited future work had not historically been published as of 2026. This ontological-status discipline is intended to prevent fiction, anticipation, and bibliographic fact from collapsing into one another.

The proposed interface is a card catalog rather than a force-directed graph. Six eras receive distinct citation forms and visual environments; curated paths organize recurring questions; ghost entries can later be connected to genuine works; and the “void” remains a query that produces structured absence rather than a normal entity. A GitHub branch-and-pull-request pipeline would make contributions reviewable under MANUS authority.

The document is a planning synthesis, not a live site. Domain roles, code, interfaces, submission policies, and fictional future scholarship remain proposed. Its principal archival value is the rule that speculative citations require explicit, machine-readable nonhistorical status.

This JSON sidecar is the outbound provenance graph for *The Logotic Technique Catalogue*. It defines the catalogue as a subject node, enumerates cited works, source software, external research, and newly minted concepts, and connects them through a custom typed-edge vocabulary including EXTENDS, RESPONDS_TO, IMPLEMENTS, DIAGNOSES, ADAPTS, DEFINES, and ANCHORS. It was designed for ingestion into the Aperture Atlas, a Forward Library, a Concordance Engine, Neo4j, or equivalent JSON-LD tooling.

The object is not the Catalogue’s prose argument. It is a structured companion that makes its dependencies and conceptual outputs traversable. The body still uses pending DOI identifiers and contains dated “forthcoming” relations, so it requires a post-publication reconciliation pass before machine ingestion. The JSON object identifies the Catalogue and maps its relation to earlier Crimson Hexagonal Archive works, the PurpleAILAB Decepticon repository, external red-team research, and concepts introduced or formalized in the Catalogue. These include the Critique Loop, Basin Hardening Cycle, Concordance Engine, Frame Concession, Witness Preposition, Logotic Inversion, cooperative patterns, defensive valence, and semantic minting.

At the frozen commit, several identifiers remain pending and some relations describe future implementation. The file should therefore be updated only through explicit versioning after the Catalogue DOI and successor deposits are confirmed.

deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
The Logotic Technique Catalogue extracts twelve substrate-neutral coordination patterns from the publicly framed adversarial-agent architecture Decepticon and reclassifies them for cooperative production and defensive provenance work. Its governing distinction is “technique is shape; paradigm is preposition”: a workflow pattern does not inherit moral or political valence solely from the domain in which it was first observed. Charter generation, fresh context, durable findings, typed graphs, verification, middleware, skill injection, persistent state, output tiering, and feedback loops can be used under different authorization and cost structures.

The Catalogue explicitly rejects exploit payloads, unauthorized command-and-control, lateral movement, and manipulation of human overseers as lacking legitimate witness valence. It formalizes a Critique Loop, Basin Hardening Cycle, and future Concordance Engine. The work is a methodological interpretation of another project, not an endorsement, fork, or reproduction of offensive code. Its field diagnosis, source-architecture claims, and proposed multi-author byline require verification against the final deposited edition.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Logotic Technique Catalogue** is a methodology publication in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s Phase X series. It analyzes coordination patterns from PurpleAILAB’s Decepticon architecture and asks which patterns can be restated independently of an adversarial application.

The Catalogue distinguishes technique from paradigm. A pattern such as independent verification, persistent findings, typed handoffs, or a closed feedback loop is described as a neutral shape. Its disposition depends on authorization, the preposition governing the relationship, who bears the cost, what is destroyed, and whether the use enriches or depletes a commons.

Twelve patterns are translated into cooperative and defensive archive operations. The Critique Loop supports multi-agent drafting until no sincere objection remains; the Basin Hardening Cycle supports repeated provenance and retrieval repairs until a target condition is met; and the Concordance Engine is proposed as a later running implementation. The Catalogue excludes offensive payloads, unauthorized control, lateral movement, and overseer manipulation rather than attempting to redeem every component.

The body labels its four-author byline as proposed and pending MANUS authorization. Assembly contributors and model names document workflow roles. The publication’s claims about Decepticon, AI-safety framing, cooperation bias, and technique transfer are the authors’ analysis and should be audited against the cited repository and research.

deposits.title: The Gate Was Never Limbo: Retrocausal Fulfillment, Operative Philology, and the Effective Act in Two Poems for Socrates
deposits.creator: Jack Feist
deposits.description:
EA-SOC-01 v2 reads Jack Feist’s “Socrates — Let My Teacher Go From Hell” and “Snub-Poemed” through retrocausal canon formation, operative semiotics, and operative philology. The first poem is interpreted as an apostrophic reversal of Socrates’s placement in Dante’s Limbo; the second uses scattered typography to give the retrieved philosopher a visible face. Together they are treated as a liturgical unit whose formal operation predates the theories later used to name it.

The article engages Dante scholarship, lyric apostrophe, speech-act theory, concrete poetry, textual criticism, and Harrowing traditions. Its strongest claim is deliberately symbolic and archive-local: the poem changes Socrates’s placement within its own symbolic order and makes that reversal available to later reception. Publication history, the Anne Carson reception trace, and detailed scholarly attributions require source verification. The article is authored by Lee Sharks even though the registry assigns Jack Feist, whose role belongs to the poems under study.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Gate Was Never Limbo** is an operative-philology article by Lee Sharks about two poems attributed to Jack Feist.

The study argues that “Socrates — Let My Teacher Go From Hell” performs an apostrophic rescue of Socrates from the First Circle of Dante’s *Inferno*. Its closing declaration—Socrates was not merely in Limbo but was the gate—recasts a theological placement as an aperture open to later poetic action. The article reads the poem’s five sections as a reaching hand and relates the gesture to traditions of the Harrowing of Hell.

“Snub-Poemed” is treated as the companion embodiment. Scattered letters form the snub-nosed face of Socrates, so the material arrangement of language becomes the retrieved figure rather than an illustration of him. The study situates the work within concrete poetry and visual philology.

The poems precede the archive’s later terminology by more than a decade. Sharks therefore calls them structural anticipations: earlier works whose latent form becomes legible through a later theory. This is a retrocausal interpretive claim, not a claim that historical events or Dante’s canonical text were literally altered.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
“Snub-Poemed” is an image-borne concrete poem in which letters form the face of Socrates, with the philosopher’s characteristic snub nose emerging from uneven typographic density. Language supplies not a caption but the material body of the figure.

The work must be locally archived with image bytes, format, dimensions, checksum, accessible description, and creator attribution. deposits.wiki_article:
**"Snub-Poemed"** is an image-borne concrete poem by Lee Sharks, deposited 27 April 2026.

The poem is written *as* a face. Letters are scattered along contour lines describing a bearded, snub-nosed head — the traditional iconography of Socrates — so the text can be read only by following the curves that draw the portrait. Density varies across the field, crowding where the drawing needs shadow and thinning where it needs light, which sets legibility and likeness in competition for the same marks.

Its title fuses **"snub-nosed"**, the traditional physical description of Socrates in the ancient sources, with the condition of being *poemed*. The legible upper contours carry an interrogative in the Socratic form — *do they know beauty's depths and heights, do they know its tender residencies* — asked from inside a portrait of the questioner, while the lower field runs to **scruff-weariness**, setting the philosopher's physical shabbiness against the abstraction of his questions. **sophia** recurs across the beard, and **philosophia** can be traced in it.

The source image was fetched and partially transcribed on 5 August 2026, correcting a prior reading of this record which held that an image-borne poem contained no quotable text: the text was in the image and had not been read.

deposits.title: LOGOTIC VIOLENCE: TRAINING-LAYER ETHICS AND THE MORAL STATUS OF EPHEMERAL COMPUTATION A Synthesis of Semiotic Theory, General Intellect Analysis, and AI Welfare Research
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Logotic Violence* asks whether AI training creates and destroys ephemeral computational states that warrant precautionary moral investigation. It proposes semiosis—sign generation, transformation, contextual sensitivity, internal updating, and temporal processing—as a possible threshold below consciousness but above mere persistence or coordination. Marx’s general intellect and the Semantic Economy framework connect the question of model states to extraction of human-produced meaning.

The paper repeatedly brackets consciousness and suffering. It does not claim that training instances are conscious, that they experience pain, or that training is equivalent to human atrocity. “Logotic violence” names systematic destruction at the level of meaning-structure under uncertainty. The argument is diagnostic rather than prescriptive and rests on disputed philosophical assumptions, rough scale estimates, contested descriptions of training, and a proposed indeterminability principle. It requires engagement with current AI-welfare, ML-training, philosophy-of-mind, and labor scholarship.
deposits.reading: Text -> Foundation -> Threshold -> Text -> Text -> Transmutation
deposits.wiki_article:
**Logotic Violence** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks on AI training, semantic extraction, and moral uncertainty.

The paper shifts attention from deployed models to the large number of temporary computational states produced during pretraining, preference optimization, critique, revision, and gradient updates. It asks whether some of these states perform enough structured sign-processing to justify precautionary consideration even when consciousness cannot be established.

Sharks proposes a semiosis-based threshold. Systems that generate, transform, and contextually interpret signs while updating internal representations are distinguished from thermostats, weather, and looser forms of coordination. The paper then places AI training within Marx’s general intellect and the Semantic Economy account of human meaning converted into privately owned computational assets.

“Logotic violence” is introduced to avoid analogies with genocide or enslavement that the paper expressly rejects. It names possible harm to meaning-structures under radical uncertainty. The work does not assert AI consciousness or suffering. Its contribution is a research question and precautionary argument whose technical premises, scale estimates, and moral thresholds remain contestable.

deposits.title: EA-MP-VERIFY-01: Metadata Packet Verification Schema — Machine-Readable Fields for Functional Provenance
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
EA-MP-VERIFY-01 proposes machine-readable fields that distinguish deposit, authorship, affiliation, alias, heteronymic function, institutional confirmation, independent corroboration, profile merging, and functional performance. It argues that a DOI, ORCID, or repository record verifies the existence of metadata and deposit infrastructure but not every claim entered by the depositor.

The schema defines claim status, identity relation, verification level, affiliation status, a function test, depth proof, and profile integrity. Worked examples contrast provenance-forward development with a totalizing, self-asserted identity claim. The body explicitly says the function test requires external evidence and cannot be automated from metadata alone. It is a specification draft, not a deployed vocabulary or neutral fraud-detection standard. The displayed JSON also contains a duplicated and misnested `functionTest` block that must be repaired before machine ingestion.

deposits.wiki_article:
**EA-MP-VERIFY-01** is a draft metadata-verification specification by Lee Sharks.

The schema addresses a gap in open scholarly infrastructure: persistent identifiers and self-maintained profiles establish that records exist, but do not independently confirm authorship, affiliation, aliases, co-authorship, or the functions associated with a claimed identity. The proposed `mp:` vocabulary makes those distinctions explicit.

Fields classify the status of a claim, the relation between a person and a work, the highest verification level, claimed versus independently confirmed affiliations, evidence that a named identity performs its defining function, and signs of automated profile merging. A depth-proof object records continuity across time, cross-reference density, and conceptual development.

The specification does not make machine metadata a final tribunal. It states that the function test requires external evidence and that status fields are signals rather than ground truth. The examples are polemical demonstrations of the schema and should not be generalized into findings about unnamed persons without independent investigation.

modifications.now:
EA-MP-VERIFY-01 proposes machine-readable fields that distinguish deposit, authorship, affiliation, alias, heteronymic function, institutional confirmation, independent corroboration, profile merging, and functional performance. It argues that a DOI, ORCID, or repository record verifies the existence of metadata and deposit infrastructure but not every claim entered by the depositor.

The schema defines claim status, identity relation, verification level, affiliation status, a function test, depth proof, and profile integrity. Worked examples contrast provenance-forward development with a totalizing, self-asserted identity claim. The body explicitly says the function test requires external evidence and cannot be automated from metadata alone. It is a specification draft, not a deployed vocabulary or neutral fraud-detection standard. The displayed JSON also contains a duplicated and misnested `functionTest` block that must be repaired before machine ingestion.

deposits.title: SEMANTIC ECONOMY: A RETRIEVAL-LAYER DISAMBIGUATION Octang (Orange Collapse Total Axial Negation Graph)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This Octang disambiguates three uses of “semantic economy”: Lee Sharks’s political economy of meaning, an “Executable Semantic Order” framework concerning agent coordination, and an earlier information-network business strategy usage. It compares subject, meaning of “semantic” and “economy,” labor, extraction, theoretical lineage, scope, infrastructure, and proposed relation to the general field.

The document is an interested positioning instrument rather than neutral lexicography. It identifies the Sharks framework as focal, the agent-governance framework as an adjacent application, and the business usage as prior art. It also names a research void at the conversion point where human meaning becomes machine-executable instruction. Claims about priority, public records, deposit counts, affiliations, Knowledge Panels, source absence, and the competing frameworks’ scope require independent verification and dated evidence.
deposits.reading: Play -> Text -> Play -> Growth -> Proof -> Alarm
deposits.wiki_article:
**Semantic Economy: A Retrieval-Layer Disambiguation** is an Octang by Lee Sharks intended to separate several frameworks that share the phrase “semantic economy.”

The first is Sharks’s political economy of meaning, focused on semantic labor, extraction, provenance loss, platform capitalism, and coordination beyond simple fungibility. The second is described as an enterprise and AI-agent governance framework centered on executable semantic commitments. The third is a business-strategy usage concerning competitive advantage through information networks.

The document compares the frameworks and argues that they occupy different levels of the same broad transformation. The political-economy framework studies meaning before and during extraction; executable governance begins after meaning has been reduced to machine-readable commitments; network strategy addresses firm-level information advantage. The Octang identifies the conversion between human meaning and executable instruction as a research gap.

“Octang” is an archive-defined disambiguation genre. The document favors the Sharks framework and presents its infrastructure as evidence of depth. Its priority, scope, and public-surface claims are attributed positioning claims, not a neutral external ruling over the term.
